thread:
alex_h: Running a perfetto + nsys pass on int8 quantized run — warm KV cache then forced eviction to reproduce the host-copy spike. Noticed big CPU->GPU memcpy bursts mid-request.

maria-ml: can you drop the trace link and the exact config? curious if it's dequant on host or weight reupload. :thinking:

alex_h: uploaded: https://perfetto.redwood/internal/trace/1779991234 (private). Config: model=redwood-7b, quant=int8-v2, batch_policy=auto, seq_len=1024, kv_cache=LRU(max_entries=120k), kernel_selector=opt_v3. Steps: warm with repeated prompts, then force-evict by calling cache.evict(older_than=5m).

devon_r: Quick skim of the perfetto timeline — at ~52ms there's a 6.4MB cudaMemcpy from host->device that aligns with a 0.9ms CPU-side dequant loop. Looks like dequant is happening on host then we memcpy weights back for that shard.

alex_h: here's the nsys sample command I ran:
```
nsys profile --output=trace_1779991234 --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=none --capture-range=cudaApi --kill=100000 --target-processes=all 
-- python benchmarks/serving_run.py --model redwood-7b --quant int8-v2 --batch auto
```
Attached flamegraph and kernel timeline under the trace dir.

perfbot: perf artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/trace_runs/1779991234.tar.gz (sha256: abc123...)

maria-ml: From kernel logs: kernel_selector logged `matmul_int8_fused selected=false` and fallback to `matmul_fp32_generic`. Selector reason: avg_seq_len=720 > threshold(512). That explains extra host work — int8 path has sequence-length specific kernels.

devon_r: That matches — when selector falls back, dequant path triggers host-side dequant for embeddings then memcpy. Also see small batch sizes (1-2) during the eviction window so fused int8 kernels aren't getting full occupancy.

alex_h: patch idea: make selector consider per-batch seq_len distribution (p90) instead of avg, and add a fast-path that keeps int8 kernel if KV cache hit ratio > 0.8. Also propose async host-dequant + prefetch to pinned memory to reduce blocking memcpy.

maria-ml: agree. Also run a microbenchmark: pin memory -> dequant -> cudaMemcpyAsync into stream 1, then launch kernel on stream 1. If that removes blocking on default stream we probably fix the spike. Can you run quick repro?

alex_h: will run pinned-mem variant tonight and post results. If it helps, kernel build v3 introduced a reorder that made the int8 kernel only take arm of weight layout A; fallback happens for layout B. Maybe we need a lightweight weight-layout adapter on the host to avoid reuploads.

ci-bot: created perf issue #452: "host memcpy spike during KV-evict causes int8 fallback" assigned to @alex_h and @maria-ml.

maria-ml: thanks — if pinned-mem reduces 95th latency we can ship selector tweak as hotfix. Also add telemetry to record kernel_selector decisions per request so we can correlate with KV hit rates. :thumbsup:

alex_h: quick summary: root cause likely selector fallback + host dequant + small batches during eviction window. Next steps: pinned-mem test, selector p90 change, telemetry for selector+kv_hit. I'll post results in the thread.

devon_r: FYI added a perfetto bookmark at 52ms in trace for team to inspect.

alex_h: posting results shortly — thanks all.
